{{Current events|year=2020|month=01|day=29|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (November 2019–present)]]
**The [[Syrian Army]] say that the [[Syrian Armed Forces|armed forces]] are now in full control of the city of [[Maaret al-Numan]], after they entered it yesterday with little resistance. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200129-syrian-army-takes-over-key-idlib-town-from-rebels-assad-damascus-aleppo (France24)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Mali]]'s [[Prime Minister of Mali|Prime Minister]] [[Boubou Cissé]] announces that his country will increase the size of its [[Malian Armed Forces|armed forces]] by 50% in recruitment to uproot [[jihadist]] groups. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security-army/mali-plans-to-increase-the-size-of-its-army-to-rein-in-jihadists-idUSKBN1ZS2ZG (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*The [[British government]] announces that rail firm [[Northern (train operating company)|Northern]] will be [[Nationalization|nationalized]] following public outcry over [[Arriva UK Trains]] handling of the firm. Arriva says it "understood the government's decision", but blames problems on "external factors" such as rail infrastructure. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-51298820 (BBC)]
*[[Facebook]] agrees to pay [[U.S. dollar|US$]]550 million to settle a [[class action]] lawsuit launched in 2015 over its mass harvesting of [[Biometrics|biometric]] data in the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Illinois]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/29/technology/facebook-privacy-lawsuit-earnings.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*In the [[Indian state]] of [[Maharashtra]], two vehicles collide and plunge into a well, killing 26 people and injuring 32 others. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-accident/twenty-six-killed-in-india-as-bus-plunges-into-well-idUSKBN1ZS1IF (Reuters)]
*Thirteen people are injured in a fire at a high rise apartment building in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], United States. [https://ktla.com/2020/01/29/fire-erupts-at-high-rise-apartment-building-near-brentwood-for-2nd-time-since-2013/ (KTLA)]

;Health and environment
*[[France|French]] Agriculture Minister [[Didier Guillaume]] announces that the [[Chick culling|culling of unwanted male chicks]] will be outlawed by the end of 2021, becoming one of the first countries to initiate such a ban. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-51301915 (BBC)]

;International relations
*[[Algeria–Bangladesh relations]]
**[[Algeria]] reopens its [[embassy]] in [[Dhaka]], after closing it in 1990. [https://www.newagebd.net/article/97994/algeria-reopens-embassy-after-3-decades-of-closure (''New Age'')]
*[[Brexit]]
**The [[European Parliament]] votes 621–49 to pass the [[European Union (Withdrawal Agreement) Act 2020|2020 Brexit agreement]], making today the last day Britain will be represented in the EU Parliament. [[Member of the European Parliament|MEP]] and Brexit campaigner [[Nigel Farage]] applauds its passage by saying "we'd be better off out", while [[Labour Party (UK)|UK Labour]] MEP [[Judith Kirton-Darling]] tearfully states it "attacks the very foundation of our identity". [https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-britain-eu-parliament/tears-and-cheers-as-eu-lawmakers-give-final-nod-to-brexit-idUSKBN1ZS1EE (Reuters)]
